title: perfcheck names_successor still lets a dropped test excuse itself by its module stem or a call form of its name
goal: names_successor skips the forms of a dropped id's own names that is_own misses: the test module's stem (test_audit, for a dropped test of that module), the test name written as a call (test_x()) and the name with a trailing space inside the backticks, beside the live-module-calls-went-with phrase; a genuine successor (a removed module's name) still counts

run: import sys,tempfile; sys.path.insert(0,'_tools'); import perfcheck; d=tempfile.mkdtemp(); r=perfcheck.names_successor('live-module calls went with `test_audit`', ['_tools/test_audit.py::test_x'], d, ''); print(r); sys.exit(1 if r else 0)

import sys;sys.path.insert(0,"_tools");import perfcheck as p;i=["_tools/test_audit.py::test_x"];ph="live-module calls went with ";bad=[t for t in ("`test_audit`","`test_x()`","`test_x `","` test_x`") if p.names_successor(ph+t,i,".","")];print(bad);sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)

import sys;sys.path.insert(0,"_tools");import perfcheck as p;i=["_tools/test_audit.py::test_x"];ph="live-module calls went with ";got=[p.names_successor(ph+"`autopilot.py`",i,".",""),p.names_successor(ph+"`test_audit` and `autopilot.py`",i,".","")];print(got);sys.exit(0 if all(got) else 1)

clauses.clause: a genuine successor (a removed module's name) still counts
